At 255 PM MST, radar indicated strong thunderstorms were located
along a line extending from 11 miles southwest of Pine Mountain to
near Tonto Basin to 8 miles south of Globe. Movement was southwest at
10 mph.

Conditions are becoming more favorable for the development of
additional thunderstorms. Some storms may become strong to severe.

Wind gusts up to 50 mph will be possible.

Locations impacted include...
Scottsdale, Globe, Superior, Hayden, Christmas, Sugarloaf Mountain,
New River, Sycamore Creek, Ballantine Trailhead, Roosevelt, Round
Valley, Sunflower, Cave Creek, San Carlos, Carefree, Miami, Cutter,
Roosevelt Dam, Top-Of-The-World, and Canyon Lake.

This includes the following highways...
AZ Interstate 17 between mile markers 231 and 239.
US Highway 60 between mile markers 219 and 282.
AZ Route 87 between mile markers 197 and 229.

Torrential rainfall is also occurring with these storms, and may
cause localized flooding. Do not drive your vehicle through flooded
roadways.

Frequent cloud to ground lightning is occurring with this storm.
Lightning can strike 10 miles away from a thunderstorm. Seek a safe
shelter inside a building or vehicle.

properties.title: Flash Flood Warning issued July 25 at 3:49PM MDT until July 25 at 5:45PM MDT by NWS Albuquerque NM
properties.description:
At 349 PM MDT, Doppler radar and automated rain gauges indicated
thunderstorms producing heavy rain over the South Fork Burn Scar. Up
to 1.5 inches of rain have fallen. Additional rainfall amounts up to
0.1 inches are possible in the warned area. Flash flooding is ongoing
or expected to begin shortly.

Excessive rainfall over the burn scar will impact Upper Canyon, Brady
Canyon, and Perk Canyon as well as the Cedar Creek, Eagle Creek and
Rio Ruidoso drainages. Impacts will include but are not limited to
all nearby reservoirs, bridges, culverts and roadways. Impacts to
areas along the Rio Ruidoso may extend downstream of Ruidoso Downs.
The debris flow can consist of rock, mud, vegetation and other loose
materials.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms producing
flash flooding in and around the South Fork Burn Scar.

SOURCE...Radar and automated gauges. A rain gauge on the South Fork
burn scar measured 1.21 inches in 30 minutes.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of areas in and around the
South Fork Burn Scar.

Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Ruidoso, Ruidoso Downs, Alto, Glencoe and Hollywood.
properties.instruction:
This is a life threatening situation. Heavy rainfall will cause
extensive and severe flash flooding of creeks, streams and ditches in
the South Fork Burn Scar. Severe debris flows can also be anticipated
across roads. Roads and driveways may be washed away in places. If
you encounter flood waters, climb to safety.
